definitions.explanation: A piece of furniture or shelving unit used to store and organize shoes, typically placed in the entryway.

examples.japanese: {玄関|げんかん}に{靴棚|くつだな}を{置|お}いた。
examples.english: I put a shoe rack in the entryway.

examples.japanese: {靴棚|くつだな}がいっぱいになってしまった。
examples.english: The shoe rack has become full.

examples.japanese: {組|く}み{立|た}て{式|しき}の{靴棚|くつだな}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought an assembly-style shoe rack.

notes:
A shoe storage shelf, typically placed in or near the {玄関|げんかん} (entryway) of a Japanese home.

FORMS:
{靴|くつ} (shoes) + {棚|たな}→だな (shelf). The {棚|たな} undergoes rendaku (voicing) to become だな in this compound.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {靴棚|くつだな}に{靴|くつ}を{入|い}れる: to put shoes on the rack
- {靴棚|くつだな}を{整理|せいり}する: to organize the shoe rack
- {組|く}み{立|た}て{式|しき}の{靴棚|くつだな}: assembly-style shoe rack

ALTERNATIVE TERMS:
- {靴箱|くつばこ}: shoe box/cabinet (more enclosed, with a door)
- {下駄箱|げたばこ}: shoe cabinet (traditional term from the geta era, still widely used)
- シューズラック: shoe rack (loanword)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Since shoes are always removed at the entrance of Japanese homes, having proper shoe storage at the {玄関|げんかん} is essential.
